title: Jolt: Using CharacterBody3D.apply_floor_snap onto an AnimatableBody3D can cause catapulting
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.6.dev2.official [7864ac801]
- Reproducible in: v4.5.1.stable.official [f62fdbde1]
- Reproducible in: v4.4.stable.official [4c311cbee]


### System information

Godot v4.5.1.stable - Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) 13 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 7600 (RADV NAVI33) - AMD Ryzen 5 7600 6-Core Processor (12 threads) - 30.50 GiB memory

### Issue description

When using Jolt physics, if a `CharacterBody3D` has a small positive velocity in the Y axis (even negligibly so), and uses `apply_floor_snap` onto a surface which is a moving `AnimatableBody3D`, then the next `move_and_slide` appears to add the surface's velocity to the character's `velocity`.  This means that, if you have a character which uses `velocity = velocity.move_toward(...)` to give a sense of inertia, the result can be that the character is rapidly accelerated in the direction of the surface's motion!

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/cab2a086-5a31-42c3-9fc9-9afeb3053db8

#### Workaround

In my experience so far, avoiding the issue needs only for the `velocity.y` to be explicitly zeroed. I do this every physics frame when the character is on the floor:

```gdscript
if is_zero_approx(velocity.y):
    velocity.y = 0
```

### Steps to reproduce

Example code from the MRP:

```gdscript
extends CharacterBody3D

const SPEED = 6.0

func _ready() -> void:
	velocity.y = 0.0000002
	
func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	var target_velocity = Vector3.LEFT * SPEED
	velocity = velocity.move_toward(target_velocity, SPEED * delta)
	apply_floor_snap()
	move_and_slide()
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[floor_snap_catapult.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23290029/floor_snap_catapult.zip)
